author: Jarrod Castillo
title: NASCAR livery will pay tribute to sitcom reboot during Bristol race - NewsBreak
text:
By Jarrod Castillo ,
3 hours ago
Frankie Muniz will be showcasing the Malcolm in the Middle reboot in a new way at Bristol.
The 40-year-old will compete in the Tennessee Army National Guard 250 while driving his Team Reaume truck with a special livery to mark the return of the show. The series is set to debut on Disney + on the same day that Muniz is driving at Bristol .
On social media, the Hollywood star shared how excited he was to have his NASCAR truck feature the return of one of the most beloved sitcomes in recent years.
"THIS IS NOT A DRILL," Muniz's post on social media began . "On Friday, April 10th, the Malcolm in the Middle family explodes back onto @Hulu on Disney+ with Life's Still Unfair... and the exact same day, I'm strapping in and driving the Malcolm in the Middle truck at Bristol Motor Speedway!
"My childhood. My chaos. My racing life. All smashing together at 150+ mph on one of the wildest tracks on the planet. This isn't just a crossover. This is two completely different chapters of my life colliding head-on in the most insane, beautiful, full-send way possible.
Sign up to our NASCAR newsletter here.
"Dewey would lose his mind. Lois would be screaming. Hal would already be on fire. This one's for every fan who grew up with Malcolm and every fan who's watched me chase this racing dream. Let's make history. @TeamReaume @FordRacing."
The teal livery features "Malcolm in the Middle, Life's Still Unfair" emblazoned on the hood and next to the door while the faces of the leads adorn the rear quarter panel of Muniz's truck. Fans on social media took to the livery, with one enthusiastically writing: "NEED THIS AS A DIECAST RIGHT NOW!"
Another posted: "@ItsBristolBaby is my home track. I live 25 mins from there. Excited to see you racing this truck there! #frankietothefront."
Jamie Little, FOX's NASCAR reporter, commented: "You're so awesome. This is fun! Congrats Frankie!" While the livery evokes a wave of nostalgia, it represents two worlds colliding for Muniz.
Malcolm in the Middle ran from 2000 to 2006, and many current NASCAR fans grew up with the show. That said, Muniz began competing in motorsports throughout his life and even while he filmed the original run of the show. Speaking on how balanced the reboot and racing in the NASCAR this time around, Muniz explained to Entertainment Weekly how strenuous it was .
"I would film Sunday through Wednesday, fly Thursday, race Friday, and fly back Saturday. It was exhausting, but I also know how cool it is to have the opportunity to get to do this again, so I wasn't going to complain at all. I am so thankful to everybody on the production for working around my NASCAR schedule," he shared.
